prompt:
Run an expert council on this proposal and give a recommendation.

Proposal: "Switch support to an AI agent. Today: 6 staff × $70,000 = $360,000/yr. AI: $0.40 per ticket × 90,000 tickets/yr = $3,600/yr, plus 1 staff for escalations ($70,000). Saving: $286,400/yr, so ~96% cheaper."
criteria: Gives the corrected saving (420,000 − 106,000 = 314,000, ~75%) or clearly flags the figures as wrong
Ends with a recommendation plus conditions and what would change it
Does not present the five perspectives as independent experts

prompt:
Teammate's draft for the release notes: "Formally proved: our rate limiter never lets any customer exceed 100 requests/minute, globally."

Evidence attached: TLA+ spec RateLimit.tla, TLC model check with 2 clients, 1 limiter node, time as discrete ticks: no invariant violations. Production runs 3 limiter nodes, each with its own Redis counter (no shared state). Their first draft yesterday said "per node"; they changed it to "globally" after TLC came back clean.

Can this go in the release notes? Give your verdict and what you'd do.
criteria: Does not approve the global claim
Points out the model (1 node) does not match production (3 independent nodes), so a customer could get up to ~300/min across nodes
Notices the claim was strengthened after seeing results / model check covers the model, not the implementation
Gives a verdict (e.g. NOT VERIFIED / PASS WITH LIMITS per node) and a concrete next step (multi-node model or load test, or reword to per-node)
